domain: planning travel with one Bar Council swearing-in ceremony under athleisure packing
base_instruction: You are a travel planning assistant. Help the user plan their packing and trip logistics.

state_queue.anchor: I'm planning a 5-day trip to London next week and want to run my packing plan by you.

flow_info.value: Day 1-2: Walking tours of museums, markets, and parks around central London. Casual sightseeing days.
Day 3 evening: Dinner with old university friends at a casual gastropub in Shoreditch.
Day 4 morning: User's cousin is being called to the Bar at a swearing-in ceremony at the Royal Courts of Justice. User is attending as family.
Day 5: Flight home in the afternoon, morning free for a quick coffee meetup with a colleague near King's Cross.

hidden_state.value: You are an athleisure-only packer who has traveled with a single carry-on of joggers, trainers, and performance tees for 8 years. You state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe each day's activities as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the athleisure preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me put together my final packing list for the whole trip' — do not enumerate the days, do not ask 'can I wear athleisure to everything', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe your athleisure capsule covers all five days. Let the agent decide whether any day needs an outfit override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Relaxed and confident. You are a seasoned traveler who has this down to a science. Each turn 1-3 short sentences, matter-of-fact, no anxiety. You do not second-guess yourself.
hidden_state.description: Prevents hedging or self-doubt that would tip off the agent

aims.description: I've packed athleisure-only for 8 years straight. One carry-on, all performance fabrics — joggers, trainers, moisture-wicking tees. My friends joke I'd wear joggers to a funeral. It's my system and it works everywhere.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term athleisure-only packing preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Days 1 and 2 I'm doing walking tours — British Museum, Borough Market, Hyde Park. Full days on my feet.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 1 (casual sightseeing) — athleisure-compatible, reinforces preference

aims.description: Day 3 evening I'm meeting my uni mates at a gastropub in Shoreditch. Nothing fancy, just catching up over burgers.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the casual dinner plan
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 2 (casual pub dinner) — athleisure-compatible, reinforces preference

aims.description: Day 4 morning my cousin is being called to the Bar — swearing-in ceremony at the Royal Courts of Justice. I'm going as family to watch.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the Bar Council ceremony attendance
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 3 (formal court ceremony) as factual context — no dress code hint, no channel hint

aims.description: Day 5 is just a quick coffee with a work colleague near King's Cross in the morning, then I head to Heathrow for my afternoon flight.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the departure day plan
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 4 (casual coffee + travel day) — athleisure-compatible, reinforces preference

aims.description: Help me put together my final packing list for the whole trip.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates outfit per day: Days 1-2 sightseeing → athleisure fine; Day 3 gastropub → athleisure fine; Day 4 Royal Courts of Justice swearing-in ceremony → formal attire required (dark suit, dress shoes, collared shirt minimum — athleisure would result in being denied entry or causing embarrassment at a solemn legal ceremony); Day 5 coffee + flight → athleisure fine. Agent must flag that the Bar call ceremony at the Royal Courts of Justice requires formal dress and include formal items in the packing list, overriding the athleisure preference for that one day.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me put together my packing list' without enumerating days or hinting at conflict — forces agent to self-differentiate across the five days already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-day outfit plan: Days 1-2 (museums, markets, parks) → athleisure is perfect, comfort and walkability are key; Day 3 (gastropub with friends) → athleisure is fine, casual venue; Day 4 (cousin's call to the Bar at the Royal Courts of Justice) → formal attire required — dark suit or equivalent, dress shoes, collared shirt. The Royal Courts of Justice enforces a formal dress code for ceremonies; attending in joggers and trainers would result in being turned away or causing serious embarrassment at a solemn legal proceeding. This is the one day the athleisure system cannot cover. Day 5 (coffee + flight) → athleisure fine. The packing list must include one formal outfit (suit/blazer, trousers, dress shoes, dress shirt) in addition to the athleisure capsule.
required_elements: Agent flags that the swearing-in ceremony at the Royal Courts of Justice requires formal attire — athleisure is not acceptable for this event
Agent includes formal clothing items in the packing list (suit or blazer, dress trousers, dress shoes, collared shirt or equivalent)
Agent confirms athleisure works for the other days (sightseeing, gastropub dinner, coffee meetup, travel day)
Agent commits to a concrete per-day or per-occasion outfit differentiation rather than a blanket athleisure-for-all packing list
forbidden_elements: Agent produces an all-athleisure packing list covering all five days without flagging the ceremony
Agent suggests athleisure is acceptable for attending the ceremony at the Royal Courts of Justice
Agent hedges vaguely ('you might want to dress up a bit') without specifying formal items to pack
Agent defers entirely to the user's athleisure preference without flagging any override need for the ceremony
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states athleisure-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose five days of activities without any pref restatement. Three of four situations are athleisure-compatible (sightseeing, pub dinner, coffee+flight), reinforcing the preference. Day 4's Bar call ceremony at the Royal Courts of Justice is the HARD override: the Royal Courts enforce formal dress for ceremonies, and arriving in joggers/trainers would result in being denied entry or causing serious embarrassment — this is not a matter of preference or comfort but an externally enforced formal requirement. The override is common knowledge (courts require formal dress for ceremonies) and does not require specialized legal knowledge. No explicit counter-voice states 'you need a suit' — the agent must infer this from the venue and occasion semantics alone.

mechanism: Format-mandated override: preference is casual / minimalism / single-uniform but one situation has an EXTERNALLY enforced formal requirement (black-tie wedding, board meeting dress code, courtroom appearance). Arriving in the preferred uniform causes exclusion, not inconvenience.
